correctness.rationale: The stationarity is constructed from the most recent independent Poisson reset, whose age is Exp(r). Odd monotone drag confines velocity and gives \(|V|\le\Sigma A\) and \(|g(V)|\le L\Sigma A\). Decomposing \(rV/\Sigma-SrA\) into force-flip and drag terms yields the \(L^2\) and Wasserstein error bound \(\sqrt{24\lambda/r}+\sqrt6 L/r\). Separated age windows decouple, while the reset-independent orientation remains correlated; fourth-moment domination by exponential ages justifies covariance convergence. The stationary age covariance is \(e^{-rt}\); multiplying by telegraph \(e^{-2\lambda t}\) gives a centered integrated-age covariance, and the time-grid maximal inequality yields uniform \(L^2\) convergence of the rescaled displacement to the integrated telegraph signal. The finite-horizon variance follows by exact double integration. Numerical checks for tan/tanh plus linear-drag exact moment identities agree; finite simulation is corroboration, not proof. No nonlinear long-time diffusivity limit is asserted.

value.rationale: The observable is the physical displacement of a continuously propelled inertial particle whose velocity is interrupted without interrupting propulsion. The theorem identifies a concrete experimentally testable mismatch: rescaled instantaneous velocity remains Laplace with variance 2 while finite-time displacement follows a persistent telegraph trajectory, and covariance at any fixed positive lag has asymptotically half the zero-lag prefactor. It provides full finite-horizon crossover and quantitative Wasserstein convergence in two physically used nonlinear media; this is structural information absent from an inverse-square diffusivity exponent or a qualitative cusp plot.
